decision: owner changed four design points: headless default, headful only on watch/take over/share, per-user profile with save_changes, Jev optional with a fast non-Jev path
one @yuki/browser package (cdp, page, plan, decide, worker) with no yuki imports; deciders are pluggable (jev, model)
why: Jev must be optional and the default path must stay fast; one loop with two deciders beats two loops

decision: plan rewritten: headless default, headful only on watch/take over/share, one browser per user so the profile has one writer, focus emulation per tab and no bringToFront, model decider default and Jev optional
kept the delete-then-create switch; Kernel DELETE returns only after the profile save (2.9 s) and the next browser sees cookies at once, timeout reaping also saves
why: logins must survive the reaper and the mode switch with one writer

decision: recorded the gate baseline before any browser code: typecheck green, server 689/690 (dev-session times out in the full run), lint already 35 errors
why: so later failures read as old versus new

decision: merged the decision layer: candidate cut, summary, lexical and Jev ranking, model and Jev deciders, one worker loop
why: both deciders hit 5/5 on the HN goals; Jev p50 ~410 ms 1.38k tokens, Muse Spark p50 1.0-1.5 s 630 tokens

decision: browser_act and browser_run stay external but pass the trust gate as ungated, so no approval card in any run
why: owner: browser must work directly, no approval cards

decision: merged the CDP and page layer; each tab gets its own background window because a shared-window background tab got 0-1 frames per 300 ms even with focus emulation
why: reads and screenshots stalled up to 10 s in a shared window
result: HN read p50 326 ms, in-page script 11 ms, CDP round trip 206 ms

decision: page script now lists password, one-time-code and card fields as secret instead of dropping them; they are never choices, and a worker that is stuck or unsure with one on screen stops as needs_human
why: dropping them hid login walls from the worker; stopping on any secret field would halt searches on pages with a header login box

decision: merged P17-01: kept @onkernel/sdk (adds 46 KB gzipped, under the 50 KB line), one browser per user in UserDO with reaper, switch and wipe
why: measured instead of guessed; the SDK stays behind a KernelClient interface so swapping it is one file
result: suite passed in 106 s; switch 4.2-4.7 s; no key or URL in any client frame
